title: agent-platform definition inputs
description: The input set of the agent-platform capability: the installation's record and the person's choices. Everything the fileset carries derives from the record (installation.*: the registry and the installation's config.yaml.patch, read, never typed), from the fleet policy (policy.yaml: which components an owning organisation's installations run, the installations with a Slack app — where the chat gateway runs — and the gateway's shape, the connector names a target's Dex registers for a hub and the Teleport cluster) and from the shared template; a person decides whether the installation serves models, where its stateful singletons run, whether its developer portal runs the AI chat, and with what model, which repositories the portal's agent creation discovers skills in, whether the cluster-manager, the model-manager and the agent-manager commit through their GitHub Apps, and the agent-manager's skill catalog. Annotations: x-source says where a value comes from (registry: read from the installations registry or the repositories, never typed; generated: created once and read back from the checkout; person: a choice). x-feature names the consistency feature of features.yaml. x-files names the repository file each fileset key is rendered to (<name> the installation; <portalHost> the installation hosting the portal the platform's portal section is written into — its own portal, else the organisation's portal on a sibling that is not hand-kept — so a portal file is read back where the section is rendered, whichever installation's plan renders it; document the path in the file of the YAML text its keys sit in, a key with dots in it bracketed); x-readback on a person input names the file — one, or several, the first on record holding the key answering — and key its value is read back from on record (kind value, present or host). x-renders lists the key paths the input produces, prefixed by the file: configmap (agent-platform configmap-values.yaml.patch), dex-configmap (the dex-app patch), extras (extras/agent-platform/ and the MCP servers' extras), backstage:* (the portal's agent-platform Component), teleport (teleport-fleet). List indices are written [*], per-installation map keys <name>.

installation.description: The facts on record. Read from the installations registry, the installation's config.yaml.patch, the cluster App's manifest and the portals' app-configs; never typed and never in the form.

name.description: The installation's codename. Where the policy's klausGateway.installations names it, a Slack app exists for the installation and the chat gateway runs, its credentials supplied at commit; elsewhere no gateway renders.

baseDomain.description: The installation's base domain; every hostname of the platform (muster, agentgateway, dex, kagent, avatars) derives from it.

customer.description: The owning organisation as the configs repository names it; selects the policy's component list and prefixes the connector names a target's Dex registers for this hub. Where the list carries kagent, the platform Postgres, the LLM routing, kagent's model provider (the key Secret, the edge as its base URL, the output cap of a call) and the UI's credentials Secret render with it.

provider.description: The infrastructure provider; selects the connectivity chart's preset for the cluster-manager's egress to the workload clusters' API servers (clusterManager.networkPolicy.workloadClusters.provider): capa renders aws, the CAPA API server load balancers; a provider the chart has no preset for renders none, the chart's default.

private.description: Reached through Teleport: a portal on record reaches the installation's Kubernetes API through the tunnel on the portal's host (kubernetes-<name>.agent-platform.svc.cluster.local) because the installation's ingress sits on private addresses. muster then reads Dex's OIDC discovery document on a private address (the shared default derives that flag from managementCluster.private, which is false where the ingress alone is private), its MCP servers reach Dex on private addresses, muster accepts private redirect URIs and a client's metadata document on agentgateway's hostname alone (the chat gateway's client_id; muster 5.35.0 or later), and a hub brokers for it through the tunnel.

chartLine.description: The meta chart line the installation runs (agentPlatform.kagentApiV2 in config.yaml.patch selects 4): the 4 line pins the chart range, derives the managers' OAuth from the template's identity block and carries the serving slice.

musterClientId.description: The platform's Dex client id: services.muster.clientId of the installation's config.yaml.patch, else the shared default's. The template renders it; the definition uses it for the managers' OAuth on the 3 line and the live probes.

clusterIssuer.description: The cert-manager ClusterIssuer of the installation's Gateway API hosts: gatewayApi.clusterIssuer of the installation's config.yaml.patch, else the shared default's. The models Gateway of the serving slice (modelServing.enabled) gets its certificate from it: the platform runs no edge of its own whose wildcard Secret could serve the models host, so the connectivity chart renders a Certificate of the host from this issuer. Absent where neither config names one; the serving slice is then refused at plan time.

portalClientSecret.description: Whether the portal client's Secret (dex-client-backstage in Dex's namespace) is on record: the customer-portal definition's file in the installation's portal directory (management-clusters/<name>/extras/backstage/backstage/dex-client-backstage-secret.enc.yaml), or the portal client already in the installation's dex-app configmap patch. The definition references the Secret and renders no file for it, so only then does it render the portals' client backstage, its audience and its trusted peer; without it a portal that lists the installation signs in there once the customer-portal definition owns the installation's portal. The registry always reads it; the default true is the render of an Action recorded before the fact existed.

podCertificateRequest.description: Whether the cluster serves certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1 PodCertificateRequest, which kagent's Agent Substrate needs on the 4 chart line: true when the cluster App's values on record (management-clusters/<name>/cluster-app-manifests.yaml) enable the feature gates PodCertificateRequest, ClusterTrustBundle and ClusterTrustBundleProjection under cluster.internal.advancedConfiguration for the API server, the controller manager and the kubelet, or when the cluster App's chart enables them by default (giantswarm/cluster 8.3.0 and later: cluster-aws 10.3.0, cluster-azure 9.3.0, cluster-cloud-director 7.3.0) — the chart at the version the App pins, or, for a release-based App that names its release (global.release.version) and no version, at the version the release lists for the chart in giantswarm/releases, read as the person; a release that cannot be read leaves the fact false with the reason on the report. Renders nothing: a 4-line record with kagent and false is refused at plan time naming the gates and the path; true renders the live probe that discovers the API and reads rolling until it is served.

collectionsStage.description: The stage the installation's app collection follows: the <stage> of bases/collections/<provider>/stages/<stage> of the fleet's base that management-clusters/<name>/collections/kustomization.yaml names as a remote resource (stable, testing, staging, ...). Absent when the kustomization names none. Where the fleet policy's releaseCandidates.stage names it and its customers list the owning organisation, the installation runs the platform's release candidates: gitops.prereleases and the agent-platform range >=4.0.0-0 <5.0.0-0 with the release tag filter, as management-cluster-bases' testing stages do for their collections.

dexAppVersion.description: The dex-app the installation runs: spec.version of the App dex-app, from the installation's own pin — a patch on the App in management-clusters/<name>/collections/kustomization.yaml — where it has one, else from the fleet's shared base, bases/collections/shared/base/dex-app.yaml in the management-cluster-bases repository the kustomization's remote resource names, at the ref it names. Absent when neither could be read (the report carries why). Renders nothing: every Dex client renders as a referenced Secret, which dex-app takes from 3.2.0 and next to a hand-made inline secret from 3.2.2, so a version older than 3.2.2 holds the commit (commitRefused, naming the file to pin it in) while the comparison still runs; an absent version holds nothing.

hub.description: The hub installation: Giant Swarm's own managers run here and its broker releases the person's GitHub grant to the Dev Portal — the `github` grant target (grantIssuer https://github.com/login/oauth) among its broker client's audiences, which backs the portal's GitHub auth API without a GitHub App. The registry's hub, not every installation with targets: a customer aggregator brokers for its siblings but holds no GitHub grant.

agentPlatform.description: Whether agent-platform is on record for the installation: its marker, installations/<name>/apps/agent-platform/configmap-values.yaml.patch, exists in its configs repository, whoever put it there. False is a fresh enable: where the record selects the 3 chart line and the fleet policy grants the organisation a component the 4 line alone carries (the cluster-manager), the enable selects the 4 line and writes agentPlatform.kagentApiV2: true into the record (installations/<name>/config.yaml.patch) as one more file of the configs pull request, keeping every other key. An installation on record keeps the line its record selects; a record on the 3 line granted such a component is refused as before.

portals.description: The developer portals that sign people in on this installation: every portal whose gs.installations lists it, from the hub's app-config and the app-config of each customer-portal installation of the owning organisation. Each forwards the ID tokens of the Dex client it signs in through; the id of a portal's client on its host's Dex (clientId) is an audience the platform trusts on the host alone, never on another installation the portal lists; the definition renders its own client for the portals (backstage, one redirect URI per portal), which every portal is trusted by as well. An id the installation trusts besides is not the definition's: the plan keeps it in the audience list it is on record in (the dex patch's trustedPeers, the platform patch's trustedAudiences, oidc-extra-audience or the edge provider's audiences), nowhere else. The platform's portal section is written into the installation's own portal, else into the organisation's portal on a sibling that is not hand-kept (a customer aggregator's); a hand-kept sibling portal, the hub's Dev Portal, carries its own section for the installations it proxies and takes no other installation's Component.

installation.description: The installation whose management-clusters tree hosts the portal.

customer.description: The host's owning organisation; the platform's portal section is written into the installation's own portal, else the organisation's own portal, never another organisation's.

clientId.description: The id of the Dex client the portal signs in through, where the host's dex-app configmap patch (installations/<host>/apps/dex-app/configmap-values.yaml.patch) carries it: the oidc.extraStaticClients entry whose redirectURIs carry the portal's (https://<domain>/api/auth/oidc-<host>/handler/frame). The portal's app-config names the id only as a reference the chart resolves from the encrypted user-secrets. Trusted on the host alone: the client is the host's Dex's, and another installation the portal lists trusts the portal through backstage. Absent when the patch carries no such client: the portal is then trusted through backstage, and an id the installation's own patches trust stays where it is on record.

handKept.description: The portal is hand-kept: its app-config on record (management-clusters/<host>/extras/backstage/backstage/app-config.yaml) carries a literal app.extensions list of its own where a portal the customer-portal definition renders includes the shared list ($include: shared-config.yaml#extensions). Backstage and helm-controller replace lists across config files and values sources, so on a hand-kept portal the platform's Component sets none of the portal's lists (app.extensions, muster.installations) and writes its object-shaped keys only (agentPlatform.kagent.installations.<name>, backstage.extraAppConfig), which merge, and the skill repositories, a list it reads back from the portal's own app-config; elsewhere the Component is the sole source of the two lists and sets them. The portal's environment, backstage.extraEnvVars, is the portal's own on every portal: the customer-portal definition's user values carry the whole list (the avatars image source, the tunnel's NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) and the Component never sets it. The hub's Dev Portal reads true. Read, never typed: the day the customer-portal definition renders the portal the fact reads false and the Component carries the lists; that definition keeps the platform's section in the portal's app-config until the fragment on record does.

grafanaWired.description: The portal's Grafana plugin is wired: its app-config on record carries the plugin's proxy endpoint (proxy.endpoints./grafana/api), the entry the customer-portal definition renders for plugins.grafana.enabled and reads the choice back from. The plugin's dashboards card is disabled in the app until a portal switches it on through its extension list, and Backstage keeps the Component's list whole over the portal's, so where the Component owns the lists its fragment includes the shared list with the platform's section and the card (shared-config.yaml#extensionsAgentPlatformGrafanaDashboards) instead of the one without the card (#extensionsAgentPlatform). Read, never typed: switching the plugin on in the customer-portal capability changes the fact, and the next agent-platform render follows it.

handKeptChat.description: Whether the portal's own app-config carries the AI chat's aiChat block by hand, so its environment supplies the chat's key already: the agent-platform Component then renders the chat's blocks and no credentials Secret and asks for no value at commit — as it sets no list on a hand-kept portal — and a wave, which carries no supplied value, reconciles the portal. Read from the app-config on record, never typed. The key becomes the Component's when the hand-kept block goes (the customer-portal definition's planned move), through an enable of the installation alone with aiChat.anthropic.apiKey supplied; until the Component's Secret is on record the customer-portal definition keeps the key in the portal's user secrets.

installations.description: The installations the portal shows (its gs.installations) that run the agent platform on record (their enabled marker), the host among them, on a portal the customer-portal definition renders. The platform's portal section lists every one of them with the installation whose plan renders it, each under agentPlatform.kagent.installations and as a muster entry at https://muster.<baseDomain>/mcp with its own sign-in provider (oidc-<name>), by name: the same file whichever installation's plan renders it, so a plan never drops what another wrote. Empty for a hand-kept portal, which carries its own section for the installations it proxies, and for a portal none of whose installations runs the platform yet. Read, never typed.

name.description: The installation's name: its kagent entry and the name and provider of its muster entry derive from it.

baseDomain.description: The installation's base domain: its muster's URL derives from it.

chartLine.description: The chart line the portal follows: the ref its directory kustomization (management-clusters/<host>/extras/backstage/backstage/kustomization.yaml) patches onto the fleet base's backstage OCIRepository — the customer-portal definition's chart.line (>=A <B) or a tag. Before backstage 1.1.0 the portal's agent-platform plugin composes the agent's HelmRelease itself and reads the agents' Flux identity from agentPlatform.fluxServiceAccountName, which the portal section then names (kagent-flux); from 1.1.0 agents are created through agent-manager and the key is not read. Absent when the kustomization patches no ref: a plan with kagent on an installation whose hosted portal carries none, or one of another form, is refused naming the file.

federation.description: The installation's place in the fleet's token exchange, from the portals' app-configs: the hubs whose broker exchanges tokens into it, and the targets its own muster brokers for.

hubs.description: Installations whose muster is the cluster-token broker of a portal that lists this one: each renders a token-exchange client in this installation's Dex, the id the hub's credentials Secret for this installation presents — the fleet's muster-token-exchange-<name> for the registry's hub (registryHub), muster-token-exchange-<name>-<hub> for every other hub — with its secret in a referenced Secret under extras/agent-platform/secrets. The secret is one generated value with the hub's credentials Secret for this installation, in the hub's plan: a plan that would draw it here alone — creating the file, or rotating it — is refused, naming the hub's file.

registryHub.description: The registry's hub by name (the installation with installation.hub), among hubs or not: its token-exchange client in this installation's Dex carries the fleet's plain id, muster-token-exchange-<name>; every other hub's carries the hub's name too. The hub renders the same id into its credentials Secret for this installation from its own installation.hub, so the two sides agree.

connectors.description: The hubs among hubs with the facts the token-exchange connector this installation's Dex registers for each is rendered from: the hub's name, its owning organisation, its base domain — the hub's Dex, https://dex.<baseDomain>, is the connector's issuer — and whether it is the first of its organisation's hubs that broker into this installation (the registry's hub first where it is one, then by name: the order the hub side names its connector by). The connector is an oidc connector trusting that issuer, under oidc.customer.connectors next to this installation's own login connectors, which the plan keeps; its name is the policy's federation.connector.first (<customer>-simple-oidc) for the first hub and federation.connector.further (<customer>-<hub>-oidc) for every further one, the name the hub renders into its broker target and identity provider for this installation. A hub of an organisation under the policy's federation.connector.fromBase renders none: the fleet's Dex base registers its connector on every installation. An entry naming a hub not among hubs is refused at plan time.

hub.description: The hub's name, one of hubs.

customer.description: The hub's owning organisation as the registry names it: the connector's prefix, and what the policy's fromBase is matched against.

baseDomain.description: The hub's base domain from its record: its Dex, https://dex.<baseDomain>, is the connector's issuer.

first.description: The hub is the first of its organisation's hubs that broker into this installation, so its connector carries the organisation's plain name; a further hub's carries the hub's own.

targets.description: Installations this one brokers for: the portal whose cluster-token broker is this installation's muster lists them. The MCP servers each target runs (servers) join muster's list with exchange auth, the exchange at the target's Dex through the connector it registers for this hub (hubs); a private target is reached through the tunnel. On the hub (installation.hub) the broker also carries the `github` grant target.

private.description: The target's record: reached through Teleport, so this hub tunnels to it — a RemoteApp per tunnelled app on this hub and the app's tunnel entry among this hub's entries of teleport-fleet's tunnelport values; the tunnel's bots join by this hub's published service-account issuer (irsa.<base domain> on capa; another provider refuses a private target).

platformProxied.description: The hub's portal proxies the target's agent platform: the app-config of a portal this installation brokers for lists the target under agentPlatform.kagent.installations, so the portal reaches the target's kagent (the UI and API v1 behind oauth2-proxy, probed at /ping) and its agentgateway (the kagent API v2 controller's gRPC listener, probed at /healthz) through the tunnel on this hub — a private target with it is tunnelled to both. A private target the portal reaches through the kubernetes tunnel alone gets neither.

hubs.description: The hubs of this installation's organisation that broker into the target, this installation among them: the cluster-token broker of every portal on record that lists the target, of the installations the registry gives the same owning organisation, the registry's hub first where it is one, then by name. The target's Dex registers one connector per hub, and only one of an organisation's hubs can carry the organisation's plain name (the policy's federation.connector.first, <customer>-simple-oidc): the first hub listed here; every further hub of the same organisation carries its own (federation.connector.further, <customer>-<hub>-oidc). Empty, this installation alone brokers into the target and carries the plain name. A list that does not name this installation is refused at plan time.

servers.description: The groups of the MCP servers the target runs: every platform server whose extras kustomization (management-clusters/<name>/extras/<server>/kustomization.yaml) the target's management-clusters repository carries. The hub federates these alone — one mcpServers entry each and, for a private target, one tunnelled app each; a server the target does not run is never registered. A target without a management-clusters repository on record is refused.

agentPlatform.description: The target runs the agent platform (its enabled marker, installations/<name>/apps/agent-platform/configmap-values.yaml.patch, is in its configs repository), whose render there holds the Dex side of this hub's token-exchange client: the two files share one generated value and are in two installations' plans, so each names the other and a plan that would draw the value on one side alone — creating it, or rotating it — is refused, naming the other side. A target without it and without clusterMcpServers keeps the client in its Dex by hand: the hub draws its side alone and a person puts the value there.

clusterMcpServers.description: The target runs its MCP servers under cluster-mcp-servers without the agent platform (that capability's enabled marker, management-clusters/<name>/extras/mcp-kubernetes/kustomization.yaml, is in its management-clusters repository), whose render there holds the Dex side of this hub's token-exchange client in the same file the agent platform's would (extras/agent-platform/secrets/dex-client-muster-token-exchange-<name>[-<hub>]-secret.yaml): the two files name each other as with agentPlatform, so the pair keeps its value when the platform is disabled on the target and its servers stay the hub's.

brokerClientId.description: Dex client id of the hub's token-exchange broker client; registered once, read back from the hub's patch afterwards. Required on a hub.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers registered on this installation beyond the platform's own three: the MCPServer objects under management-clusters/<name>/extras/agent-platform/mcpservers/ that the directory's kustomization lists, where the tree's kustomization (extras/agent-platform/kustomization.yaml) lists the directory. A person registers a server by adding its MCPServer object there in muster's own shape — auth.forwardToken, auth.tokenExchange or auth.authorizationServer, the credentials Secret it references under ../secrets — and listing it; the platform renders nothing per server. It reads each one's state live, and where one exchanges tokens at a Dex of its own (auth.tokenExchange.dexTokenEndpoint) muster's token-exchange client is allowed to reach a private address: a workload cluster's Dex sits behind an internal load balancer, and the endpoint it is allowed for is on record. An entry of the values patch (agent-platform-mcps.mcpServers) is no registration: that list is the platform's own three and, on a hub, its targets'.

name.description: The object's name in muster's namespace (agent-platform).

url.description: spec.url: where muster reaches the server.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to the server, in the agent-platform-mcps chart's words: none; forward, the person's own ID token (auth.forwardToken); exchange, a token exchanged at another Dex (auth.tokenExchange); oauth, a grant at the server's own authorization server (auth.authorizationServer).

dexTokenEndpoint.description: For exchange: the token endpoint of the Dex the exchange runs at (auth.tokenExchange.dexTokenEndpoint).

githubGrant.description: For oauth: the server holds the person's own GitHub grant (auth.authorizationServer.issuer https://github.com/login/oauth with grantScope subject). On an installation that is neither the registry's hub nor a broker for targets and that hosts its own portal, the broker releases the grant to that portal: muster's broker gets the github grant target and the portal's broker client (backstage), muster trusts this installation's Dex as the issuer of the portal's subject tokens (an issuer on record stays as it is), and the portal's Component gets gs.github on this server, gs.clusterTokenBroker on this muster and the broker client's credentials, their secret drawn once for both Secrets. People connect GitHub on this installation, and the portal holds no GitHub App. The Hive's plans backend reads GitHub through the same server (hive.enabled).

toolPrefix.description: spec.toolPrefix: the prefix muster exposes the server's tools under (x_<prefix>_<tool>); empty, the server's name. The Hive's blocks name it where it differs from the name.

board.description: The server serves the roadmap board: pro, by muster's type label (metadata.labels muster.giantswarm.io/type: mcp-pro). The Hive's roadmap backend runs its board tools as the signed-in person (hive.enabled).

mcpClients.description: The MCP clients registered on this installation with a stable HTTPS callback — a hosted agent runtime such as AWS Bedrock AgentCore, which registers itself with muster (dynamic client registration) and publishes no client metadata document: the ConfigMaps under management-clusters/<name>/extras/agent-platform/mcpclients/ that the directory's kustomization lists, where the tree's kustomization lists the directory, each one consumer with its redirect URIs (data.redirectURIs, one per line). muster registers such a client only for a redirect URI it trusts, and the definition renders that allowlist from these registrations, in the kustomization's order. A person registers a client by adding its ConfigMap there and listing it.

redirectURIs.description: The consumer's callback URIs, fully qualified HTTPS.

modelServing.description: One choice: whether the installation serves models.

enabled.description: Serve models on this installation: the llm-d control plane, the well-known LLMInferenceServiceConfigs, the model serving switch and the models Gateway with its certificate from the installation's cluster issuer (installation.clusterIssuer) (the meta chart's serving slice, 4.44.0 and later). The 4 chart line only; the GPU pool is the cluster-manager's.

scheduling.description: One choice: where the platform's stateful singletons run.

singletonsCapacity.description: The Karpenter capacity the four stateful singletons (muster, muster-valkey, the kagent controller, klaus-gateway) run on: any (the NodePool's choice, spot included) or on-demand (karpenter.sh/capacity-type: on-demand), since a spot reclaim of their node takes muster's token store or the chat gateway away for minutes. on-demand is for a capa installation whose Karpenter NodePool admits on-demand; the pods stay Pending where no node carries the label.

aiChat.description: The other choice: the developer portal's AI chat, in the platform's portal section. The chat runs Claude on Anthropic's API (the key supplied at commit as aiChat.anthropic.apiKey) or on Vertex AI (aiChat.provider: vertex, with the Google project and location; the service account's JSON supplied at commit as aiChat.google.credentialsJson); a credential is never typed here or read back, and lands in the Component's own Secret agent-platform-ai-chat-credentials-backstage as the chart value the chart exposes as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or mounts at /app/google/credentials.json. Read back from the Component's fragment on record, else from the portal's own app-config — a hand-kept portal is read from its app-config, and its chat moves into the Component at the next reconcile.

enabled.description: The portal's AI chat: the aiChat block on the provider with its two MCP servers (the portal's own actions server at /api/mcp-actions/v1 with the signed-in person's token, the installation's muster with the sign-in provider), the actions server's tool naming (mcpActions) and the actions the service lists for it (backend.actions), the credentials Secret appended to the portal HelmRelease's values sources, and on a rendered portal the shared extension list with the chat (shared-config.yaml#extensionsAgentPlatformAiChat, or its GrafanaDashboards pair where the portal's plugin is wired); a hand-kept portal keeps its own list, which carries the chat's entries already. Read back from the block's presence.

model.description: The model the chat answers with (aiChat.model), a Claude model id the provider serves. Read back from the block on record.

provider.description: Which platform serves the chat's Claude model: anthropic, Anthropic's own API with the key from the portal's environment (aiChat.anthropic.apiKey, supplied at commit); or vertex, Claude on Google Cloud Vertex AI in the project and region of aiChat.google, authenticated from the service account's JSON (aiChat.google.credentialsJson, supplied at commit) the chart mounts at /app/google/credentials.json — the block names the provider and the file, the Component's values carry the project and location the chart exports. Read back from aiChat.anthropic.provider on record; a block without it runs on Anthropic's API.

google.description: Where a chat on Vertex AI runs; both are named with aiChat.provider: vertex and refused empty there, unread otherwise.

project.description: The GCP project Vertex AI serves the model in (aiChat.google.project, the chart's GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT). Read back from the block on record.

location.description: The Vertex AI region, a multi-region such as eu for data residency or a single region (aiChat.google.location, the chart's GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION). Read back from the block on record.

skills.description: The skill catalog of the portal's agent creation, in the platform's portal section.

repositories.description: The GitHub repositories the portal's agent creation discovers skills in (agentPlatform.skills.repositories): every SKILL.md in one is a skill the create flow offers. The Component's fragment carries the list, on a hand-kept portal too, since the list is read back from the portal's own files; none, the key is not written and the catalog is empty, the plugin's default. Read back from the fragment on record, else from the portal's own app-config — a hand-kept portal lists the repositories there, and the list moves into the fragment at the next reconcile.

hive.description: The portal's Hive section (Plans, Roadmap and the product magazine at /hive), in the platform's portal section: the plans and roadmap backends read GitHub and the board as the signed-in person through this installation's muster, so the section needs the portal hosted on this installation and two registered servers there, one holding the person's GitHub grant (installation.mcpServers[*].githubGrant) and pro serving the board (installation.mcpServers[*].board). No credential: muster holds the person's grants.

enabled.description: The Hive pages: the plans block (the plan repositories, the magazine, GitHub through the grant server on this muster) and the roadmap block (the board, its default teams, pro on this muster) in the Component's fragment, and on a rendered portal the shared extension list with the Hive's pages (shared-config.yaml#extensionsAgentPlatformHive, with AiChat before Hive where the chat is on and GrafanaDashboards after it where the portal's plugin is wired); a hand-kept portal keeps its own list, which carries the pages already. Refused where the portal is not hosted on this installation or its muster registers no grant server or no board server. Read back from the plans block's presence, in the fragment on record, else in the portal's own app-config, so a portal that carries the section by hand keeps it.

repositories.description: The plan repositories the Plans page offers, as owner/repo (plans.repositories); a person sees one only where their own GitHub account reads it. Refused empty with hive.enabled: the plans backend serves nothing without one. Read back from the block on record.

repository.description: The product magazine's repository, as owner/repo (plans.magazine.repository): its generated data on the data branch and its knowledge documents on main, the plugin's defaults. Empty, no magazine block, and the Magazine page says it is not configured. Read back from the block on record.

board.description: The board the Roadmap page serves, as pro names it (roadmap.board). Read back from the block on record.

teams.description: The teams the Roadmap page's filter shows by default, as the board names them (roadmap.teams); none, the key is not written and the filter starts empty. Read back from the block on record.

modelManager.description: One choice: the model-manager's commit mode.

enabled.description: The model-manager's commit mode through its GitHub App (model-manager.github.enabled): the chart registers with muster pinned to the App and wire_model, unwire_model and the kserve load_model and unload_model take mode: commit, the pull request opened as the person in the repository that owns the target namespace. The connectivity chart opens its egress to api.github.com (GET /user, the pull request). The App's OAuth client is the installation's own Secret, giantswarm-model-manager-oauth-client in agent-platform, not rendered. On the 4 chart line only, where the model-manager runs. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

agentManager.description: Two choices: the agent-manager's commit mode and its skill catalog.

repositories.description: The GitHub repositories agent-manager's list_skills discovers skills in (agent-manager.skills.repositories), the catalog meta agents create agents from. None, the key is not written and the chart's default (giantswarm/agent-skills) stands. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

appSecretName.description: The installation's Secret in agent-platform holding the read-only skills GitHub App's app-id, installation-id and private-key (agent-manager.skills.github.app.secretName; giantswarm-agent-skills-app by convention, not rendered): agent-manager discovers and pins skills with the App's installation tokens and offers a private repository only to the people who can read it. The Secret exists before this is set: a missing one stops the pod. Empty, anonymous discovery, public repositories only. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

gitAuthSecretName.description: The Secret in kagent (key token) every agent with a git skill fetches its skills with at boot unless it names its own (agent-manager.skills.gitAuthSecretName; kagent-skills-token, the token the GitOps agents boot with, not rendered). Empty, such agents fetch anonymously. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

mintGitAuthSecret.description: agent-manager keeps the boot Secret of git skills filled with the skills GitHub App's installation token (agent-manager.skills.mintGitAuthSecret, agent-manager 1.8.0 or newer): the chart renders agent-manager-skills-token in kagent and composes it onto every agent with a git skill, so no personal token is needed. Needs appSecretName; replaces gitAuthSecretName. Turned off, the chart removes that Secret and every agent that names it stops booting its private skills. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

enabled.description: The agent-manager's commit mode through its GitHub App (agent-manager.github.enabled): the chart registers with muster pinned to the App and create_agent, update_agent and delete_agent take mode: commit, the pull request opened as the person in the repository that owns the target namespace. The connectivity chart opens its egress to api.github.com (GET /user, the pull request). The App's OAuth client is the installation's own Secret, giantswarm-agent-manager-oauth-client in agent-platform, not rendered. Where the fleet policy runs the agent-manager only. Read back from the configmap patch on record.

clusterManager.description: One choice: the cluster-manager's commit mode.

enabled.description: The cluster-manager's commit mode through its GitHub App (cluster-manager.github.enabled): the chart registers with muster pinned to the App and create_node_pool and delete_node_pool take mode: commit, the pull request opened as the person; its egress adds api.github.com (GET /user, the pull request). The App's OAuth client is the installation's own Secret, giantswarm-cluster-manager-oauth-client in agent-platform, not rendered. Where the fleet policy runs the cluster-manager only; read back from the configmap patch on record.

versions.description: Version holds: a chart kept on a version, or a range, other than the definition's. A hold is set on record and read back from it, so a reconcile keeps it; only a typed input (--input versions.<key>=<version>, or empty to lift it) moves it. The rendered value carries a comment: the hold's reason (versions.reasons.<key>) where one is on record or typed, else the generic one naming its input.

chart.description: A hold on the agent-platform meta chart: the version or range its OCIRepository follows, in place of the chart line's range (installation.chartLine). Empty, the line's range stands. Read back from the OCIRepository patch of the extras kustomization on record; a whole major line's range there (>=4.0.0 <5.0.0, its release candidates' >=4.0.0-0 <5.0.0-0) is the line's own and reads back as no hold.

components.description: Holds on the meta chart's components, by component: each one's versionRange in the configmap patch.

muster.description: A hold on the muster chart: the version or range its HelmRelease follows (components.muster.versionRange), in place of the meta chart's. Empty, the meta chart's stands. Read back from the configmap patch on record, so a reconcile keeps it; typed, it moves or lifts it.

reasons.description: The holds' reasons, by the hold's key: the comment written above the hold in the file, as a person wrote it on record or typed it, read back so a reconcile keeps it. Empty, the hold carries the generic comment naming its input; a hold that is not set carries nothing.

chart.description: The reason of the hold on the meta chart (versions.chart): the comment above its OCIRepository patch in the extras kustomization, as a person wrote it on record or typed it (--input versions.reasons.chart=<text>, a line per line), read back so a reconcile keeps it; the generic comment naming the input reads back as none. Empty, the hold carries the generic comment.
